title: An expression the result does not need is not evaluated, and its error does not raise
description: A projection `g = CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN `error()` ELSE b END` over a table with one row where `b = 0` raises only where the query needs `g` on that row. It returns rows without raising where the column is not read, where a filter above it drops the row (pushed below the projection), where it is joined to an empty input, and under `count(*)`; it raises where the output reads `g` on every row. Under a `LIMIT` it raises only where the rows the limit keeps include that row.

So a guard inside a plan is a side effect the engine may never take: it evaluates lazily, where the reference evaluates every expression of a projection on every row of its input (`Rel.HasIssue`, `Rel.Raises`).
reference: The reference raises wherever the plan as written evaluates an operation that raises, whatever sits above it: a project raises when any expression raises on any row of its input. A report's assumed issues (an integer `SUM` that leaves 64 bits, an operation on finite doubles that gives `±∞`) are preconditions the run checks on the data.

Workaround (#2018, ruling 195): `Report._check_assumed` runs a check plan of its own (`assumedCheck`, `analysis/Sverify/Analysis/AssumedCheck.lean`), one row whose values are the verdicts, aggregates without groups at the root, which every engine computes. The in-plan guards stay as a defence.

provenance.checked_by: optimizer session, #2018 (the five shapes of ruling 195, default settings)

evidence.sql: SELECT a FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS q
SELECT a, g FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS q WHERE a > 0
SELECT a, g FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS q ORDER BY a DESC) AS r LIMIT 1
SELECT x.a, x.g FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS x JOIN (SELECT a FROM t WHERE a > 100) AS e ON x.a = e.a
SELECT count(*) AS n FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS q
SELECT a, g FROM (SELECT a, CASE WHEN b = 0 THEN error('boom') ELSE b END AS g FROM t) AS q
